specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk spatial search on a graph with N vertices, using Schrödinger evolution under a walk Hamiltonian with walking rate gamma plus an oracle term for a marked vertex; the abstract's specific graph examples and two-stage algorithm are not defined.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background single-stage continuous-time quantum walk search (Childs-Goldstone style) on a tiny explicit instance, the complete graph K_4 with one marked vertex. Out of scope: the paper's low-connectivity fast-search graph, its high-connectivity slow-search graph, the two-stage algorithm, its gamma adjustment schedule, and connectivity measures.

symbols.domain: positive integer, N=4 in the toy instance

equations.label: Schrödinger evolution
equations.description: Quantum particle evolves under Schrödinger's equation.
equations.abstract_quote: A randomly walking quantum particle evolving by Schrödinger’s equation
equations.justification: The abstract names Schrödinger evolution for the walk; the explicit form is standard.
assumptions: time-independent H in a single stage

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Walk term from the graph Laplacian plus an oracle term marking w.
equations.justification: Standard continuous-time quantum search form; the paper's exact Hamiltonian and any two-stage variant are not given.
assumptions: Laplacian-based walk; adjacency-based variants differ for irregular graphs

equations.label: Initial state
equations.justification: Usual starting state for spatial search.

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of measuring the marked vertex.
equations.justification: Born rule applied to the vertex basis.

equations.label: Fast-search scaling claim
equations.description: Runtime scaling stated for d-dimensional cubic lattices.
equations.abstract_quote: searches on $d$-dimensional cubic lattices in $O(\sqrt{N})$ time when $d\geq 5$
equations.justification: Directly stated asymptotic claim; not used to build the toy circuit.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Vertex basis |v>, with v encoded as a binary integer, most significant bit first

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition |s> over all N vertex states on the vertex register.

steps.description: Evolve under H for time T, with gamma tuned for the instance; the paper's two-stage algorithm would change gamma between stages, but that schedule is unspecified.
Measure the vertex register in the computational basis and compare the success probability to the target.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the vertex register; success means obtaining w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check whether the outcome equals w; repeat if it does not.
assumptions: Chose the smallest instance, K_4 with marked vertex w=0, as a toy example.
Single-stage Laplacian-based Hamiltonian used as a generic baseline, not the paper's method.
Optimal gamma and T are not specified; gamma=1/N is a known choice for the complete graph but is not from the abstract.
